lead.hed: A retired Marine drill instructor went back to college so his daughter could finish Vanderbilt
lead.insight: Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division said Thursday that Dwayne Fochler, a retired Marine, enrolled at the University of La Verne in 2018 after he learned he could not transfer GI Bill benefits to his daughter as a retiree. The housing allowance and book stipend went to her. He finished a bachelor's degree in 2020. She earned back what Vanderbilt cost within five years. Fochler now heads the Targets and Mission Planning Support Division at Point Mugu and received a 40-year Length-of-Service Award on Sept. 30. The official still, taken Oct. 21 and posted today, shows him with a BQM-177A aerial target in a hangar.
lead.image_credit: Tim Gantner · DVIDS 10040716 · Public domain · Dwayne Fochler leans on a BQM-177A aerial target in a hangar at Point Mugu, California. Photo dated Oct. 21, 2026, posted Oct. 22, 2026.

political.hed: Heritage says Delaware parents still need guidance on artificial intelligence in school
political.insight: Thursday's Heritage commentary says Delaware lawmakers created a committee in 2024 to study artificial intelligence, and that parents and teachers still lack usable guidance. The piece is argument about family and classroom rules. It does not reprint a bill or a floor vote.

political.hed: Law & Liberty asks whether fusionism still charts a course for conservatives
political.insight: Thursday's Law & Liberty essay takes up Frank Meyer's fusion of liberty and virtue and asks whether that bargain still holds. It is argument, not a statute or a roll call.

political.hed: Public Discourse says splitting mother from child in the talking points repeats what abortion does
political.insight: Thursday's Public Discourse essay says pro-life argument has to keep the woman and the unborn child in the same sentence. The writer says baby-only messaging leaves the mother out of the public case. It is argument. It does not cite a floor vote.

tech.hed: Theodore Roosevelt and allied ships are in the Philippine Sea for Keen Sword
tech.insight: U.S. Forces Japan said Keen Sword 27 opened Oct. 19. About 45,000 Japan Self-Defense Force personnel and 11,000 U.S. troops are in the exercise, with 260 aircraft and 40 ships, including the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group. Australia, Canada, France, New Zealand, and the Philippines are in the drills. Korea and the United Kingdom sent observers. USNI News reported Thursday that the strike group is sailing with Japanese, Australian, Canadian, and French warships in the Philippine Sea. The exercise runs through Oct. 29.

tech.hed: The Pentagon and Lockheed agreed to a 10-year frame for at least 850 F-35s
tech.insight: Defense News reported Thursday that the Pentagon and Lockheed Martin agreed to a decade-long framework covering at least 850 F-35 Lightning II fighters for the U.S. military. The buy still needs congressional approval and funding. The story does not reprint the contract.

tech.hed: Army maintenance software can now keep working offline for seven days
tech.insight: The Army said Thursday that the Global Combat Support System-Army's disconnected maintenance tool, DISCOPS, lets units keep essential work going for up to seven days when the network is down. Records sync when the link returns. The release calls it an operational milestone for units that cannot stop maintenance because the connection dropped.

culture.hed: The Old Guard fife and drum corps raised the flag at Aberdeen for America 250
culture.insight: The Army said Thursday that the Old Guard Fife and Drum Corps played an America 250 flag raising at the Combat Capabilities Development Command Chemical Biological Center on Aberdeen Proving Ground. Sgt. 1st Class Ryan Koesterer, Staff Sgt. Joshua Robbins, and Sgt. 1st Class Jeffrey Brooks took part. The official still was taken today.
